title: Landsat farm-dam levels fell with river flow in the 2002-2009 drought in 85 south-east Australian catchments, but not after 2010; a similar dam-river gap in a northern control limits attribution
abstract: Question: after 1997, south-east Australian (SE-AU) river runoff fell 20-25% below its pre-1997 relation to rain and stayed low. Does the loss occur where runoff is generated on hillslopes, or lower in the landscape? Approach: small farm dams fill from local hillslope runoff. We used Landsat water areas of 11,445 waterbodies of 0.1-5 ha (DEA Waterbodies v1, 1987-2020) inside CAMELS-AUS catchments as a gauge-free hillslope runoff index, and compared the spring dam level with river flow. Models used a 1988-1996 calibration on season rain, antecedent rain and lake evaporation; residuals are in rain equivalents. Controls: North-AU (35 catchments) and SW-WA (16). Landscape position came from the Copernicus GLO-90 DEM. Results: the planned annual test was inconclusive, because part of the deficit predates 1988. In 2002-2009, SE-AU dams and rivers fell below their rain relations together (-0.29 and -0.29 rain equivalents). In 2013-2019 dams returned to their relation (+0.07, 95% CI -0.22 to +0.32) while rivers stayed low (-0.26, -0.39 to -0.13). The upper envelope of the dam wet area did not drift between Landsat eras. But North-AU had a dam-river gap of the same size (+0.25 against +0.33), and the SE-AU gap interval included zero when the calibration years were also resampled. Across 85 SE-AU catchments, dam and river shifts correlated (rho 0.59), but only 0.21 (-0.12 to 0.47) after location and baseline controls, as for bores. Low-lying waterbodies did not lose more than elevated ones in rain-equivalent units (+0.01, -0.14 to +0.15), and the contrast did not follow the river loss. Conclusion: hillslope dams shared the drought-time loss but not the later loss, which agrees with a slow store below the hillslope; the same gap in a control region, the short baseline and farm water use prevent attribution. No valley-floor groundwater signature was found.

Blue: spring farm-dam level from Landsat. Orange/green: May-Nov river flow (log/linear). Bands: 95% cell-bootstrap intervals.

Post hoc sub-period means of dam and river residuals for SE-AU, SW-WA and the North-AU control. Dams and rivers fell together in 2002-2009 in SE-AU; after 2012 dams were at their rain relation and rivers below it, in all three regions.

Left: catchment dam-level shift against river shift (1997-2019 minus 1988-1996), coloured by longitude; the link is mainly a west-east gradient. Right: low-lying minus elevated waterbody shift against river shift; no valley-floor signature.
